computer.list.doc: Every computer: its folders' owner, OS, display, agents, level and state (§9.1).

computer.get.doc: One computer, by name or alias.

computer.setLevel.doc: Changes a computer's approval level: a sealed card unless made in the user's own terminal (§5.5); from a peer, the receiver's own level.

computer.rename.doc: Renames a computer in the tree; the old name stays as an alias.

hold.list.doc: A computer's holds and its user-working mark.

tree.stat.doc: A path's type, size and time; null when it doesn't exist.

tree.read.doc: Reads a file on the computer that holds it.

tree.write.doc: Writes a file on the computer that holds it, inside the fence; `executable` sets its mode (a new file keeps it off).

tree.move.doc: Moves within one computer; across computers the core copies, then deletes.

tree.glob.doc: Finds files on the computer that holds `cwd`; only the results travel (§9.1).

tree.grep.doc: Searches file contents on the computer that holds `cwd`.

tree.mkdir.doc: Makes a folder, and any missing above it, inside the fence.

tree.readlink.doc: A link's target, as written in the link.

tree.symlink.doc: Makes a link at `path`; the holder's fence judges the link and, when it is followed, where it leads.

tree.watch.doc: Watches a folder (a code session's, never a whole home): its changes come as `tree_changed` with this id.

tree.unwatch.doc: Ends a watch; only the computer that started it can end it.

tool.run.doc: Runs a tool call (Bash, a local MCP server's tool) on the computer that holds its folder; output streams as `tool_output`.

tool.cancel.doc: Cancels a running call; if the link is down, the holding computer stops it when the link returns (§6.4).

tree.judge.doc: Whether this holder would take its part of a move or copy at this level; refused with `NeedsAnswer` when the user's answer would lift it.

tree.receive.doc: Makes this computer the destination of a move or copy from another: it takes the files over `tree.send` and renames them into place, never over something there. `kept`: a move's entries that changed at the source meanwhile, and stay there too.

tree.sent.doc: The destination has the files in place: a move's source removes what it sent, keeping what changed meanwhile.

computer.takeHold.doc: Takes a hold on the receiver's own screen, for the calling computer's session.

computer.releaseHold.doc: Lets go of a hold the calling computer took here.

computer.releaseSession.doc: Lets go of every hold the calling computer took here for one session, at its turn's end.

computer.holds.doc: The receiver's holds and whether the user is working there.

mcp.mirror.doc: Installs an MCP server on the receiver: always the user's answer for its own card, bound to the server and its config, whatever the levels, since a server runs commands.

terminal.open.doc: Opens a terminal on a computer, in the user's shell; its output streams as `terminal_output`. A computer at read-only never opens one for a plugin (`refused`).

terminal.write.doc: What lane E's runtime derived from the user's key presses or a paste in the terminal panel.

terminal.resize.doc: The terminal's new size in cells.

terminal.close.doc: Ends the terminal's shell and closes it.

computer_changed.doc: A computer was added or changed state, level or name.

holds_changed.doc: A computer's holds or user-working mark changed.

action_running.doc: A computer-use action started or ended on a computer; the app counts no card click meanwhile.

tool_output.doc: A running `tool.run` call's output, back to the computer running the session.

tree_changed.doc: A watched folder's changes, from the computer that holds it to the one that watches (`tree.watch`).

computer_hello.doc: A computer introduces itself to a peer when a link opens and when it changes: its name, level, agents and where its part of the tree lives.

terminal_output.doc: A terminal's output; `exited` once its shell ends.
